headline: Pretrained sequence models extend to RNA structure, glycosylation, and epitopes
label: Biological Sequence Foundation Models
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair pretrained DNA, RNA, and protein language models with structure, domain, and contact information.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained sequence representations for downstream prediction across DNA, RNA, and protein. IsoAlign pretrains DNA foundation models through isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment using two JEPA variants. LIMBER, a hybrid self-attention and Mamba model, is pretrained on 40.5M ncRNA sequences, and structRFM is pre-trained on 21M sequence-structure pairs. MaskNGly applies protein language model embeddings zero-shot to N-glycosylation site prediction, matching supervised predictors. PALM adapts ESM2 with LoRA and a BiLSTM for domain, functional-site, and zero-shot missense effect prediction. What is new is the integration of structural, domain, contact, or template information with general sequence embeddings rather than sequence alone: structRFM incorporates structure, MIL-BC represents proteins as bags of detected domains for EC prediction, and CARTnet adds contact-aware attention with template epitope information.
